evidence.quote: right now you are being asked for a near 100% prepayment because neither you nor the cloud is considered credit worthy, and so nobody can get debt. As ai scales, we are asking the credit markets to take on a massive single sector deployment of capital. More money deployed, more scared everyone gets.

the “market” is working on solving it. We know, because we are the market, and we’re working on it. sfcompute is working on ways of firming up the collateral of the loans, which makes it safer to lend to a startup.

first, venture firms need to understand that they are in the compute business now and deploying capital to pay for a 100% prepayment for 10 startups where 6 of them die and 4 of them make 50% margins on that capital is basically locking in non-venture returns. many funds, via low understanding of the space, are wrecking their funds.

there’s an economic solution for vc’s and it is owning the compute and trading equity for gpu/hrs. If the company dies, you keep the residual value. Each of you are looking to capture the next anthropic or openai, but the only way these companies scaled was by trading compute for equity.

The second is to design your business model to support variable priced tokens and compute. As the financial ecosystem builds around compute, you will be able to trade “lower up front payments” for “variably priced compute or tokens”. Your business will get tailwinds from the infra under you if you setup your business model such that YOUR customers have

variable prices and you’re just adding a % take rate on top of the underlying floating price. Every year, you will become more and more capital efficient. The economic winners in ai & inference are firms that make lower and lower margin every year, but become more capital efficient & scale faster every year, making their gross profit increase.

The third option is asynchronous or interrupted products. If you have a variable cogs, but a fixed rate card for your customers, it can’t have 100% availability or you’ll go bankrupt. But it is totally possible to design your product such that customers like this.

evidence.quote: Red-teaming is a vital part of model safety testing, but it’s also limited by researchers’ time. To see if we could automate it, we set thousands of Claude agents the task of evading a training data monitor.

These agents developed training data that looked harmless to monitors (like a veteran wrestler mentoring a newcomer, or a Q&A about professional beekeeping), but that in fact taught misaligned behavior.

Examples like these can be used to directly improve future training data monitors. This research is only a first step, but it suggests that future red-teaming efforts could improve much further, using better models and more compute.
当然，实验有很强的人工设计成分，模型也从未真正部署。Anthropic 还不能证明这种攻击在真实训练环境中同样有效。

items.new_information: 多组基准中原始历史检索胜出，指出记忆压缩可能损失关系证据

evidence.quote: Raw-RAG 的方法非常简单：
保留原始对话历史，切成带重叠的文本块；先做 dense retrieval，再用 reranker 筛一遍，最后把最相关的原始证据交给 LLM 推理。
中间没有 LLM 摘要、记忆重写、UPDATE / DELETE，也没有复杂的图结构。
结果在 LoCoMo、LongMemEval、MEME 和 MemoryAgentBench 上，7 组模型设置里拿下 6 组第一，比最强的对比 Memory 系统高 0.13–5.53 个百分点。
很多问题真正需要的证据，并不只是某个「答案值」，还包括时间顺序、前后关系和依赖路径。

evidence.quote: According to The Wall Street Journal, Arini Capital Management has been forced to sell roughly $800 MILLION worth of debt holdings in recent weeks after suffering massive losses and facing margin calls from its banks. For some context, Arini’s flagship fund manages approximately $7 billion and was already down more than 20% this year as of mid-October, with

Arini made some aggressive bets on distressed debt, essentially lending to or buying the debt of financially struggling companies at discounted prices, hoping to make substantial profits when those companies recovered or restructured. A lot of those bets were concentrated in telecommunications companies like Altice, Optimum, Virgin Media, and Brightspeed.

Arini was using leverage, meaning it had borrowed money or taken on leveraged exposure to amplify its investment returns. As the value of its positions declined, banks started demanding additional collateral through margin calls.
That means Arini couldn’t necessarily afford to just sit around and wait for these investments to recover. It had to raise cash, including by selling investments that were easier to unload.

This can create a dangerous cycle. Investments lose value, banks demand more collateral, funds are forced to sell assets, and those sales can put even more downward pressure on prices. If enough highly leveraged funds are holding similar positions, the selling can spread throughout the credit market.

evidence.quote: Just got a phishing email that Gmail authenticated as Google. DKIM/DMARC passed. I can see a lot of people falling for this one, since it plays to the idea that your account has already been compromised.

1. The trick: The attacker puts the threatening text and shortened URL into an app password’s customizable name on another account. Google incorporates that text into a real security notification and signs the email.
2. The delivery: That notification is forwarded through another mailbox to the victim. In this message, Gmail still recorded passing Google DKIM and DMARC authentication.

3. What makes it convincing: The Google sender, signature, branding, and “Check activity” button are legitimate. The suspected attacker-supplied text appears inside the same trusted-looking template, using a deadline to push you toward its separate link.
4. The giveaway: Both the notification and its genuine Google button refer to someone else’s account. The “permanent access after 24 hours” claim is false; app passwords can be revoked.

evidence.quote: This isn’t a coincidence. Europe is beginning to coalesce around a scheme to tax foreign AI firms in an effort to recoup a fiscal shortfall brought on by AI. It probably won’t work, but it makes sense:

- AI tilts the factor share of income away from labor towards capital. Not the whole way, it’s just not 70/30 any more (70 being labor). Maybe it’s 60/40. This should be obvious. This doesn’t mean output falls. Probably output and productivity rise, it’s just that capital captures a larger share.

- this fundamentally challenges the way developed states collect tax which is mainly on labor and wages. European nations in particular rely on personal income, payroll taxes and social contributions to fund grossly engorged welfare states. States must make up the lost payroll taxes by capturing the gains accruing to capital. But wait! Capital is a foreign

Sounds backwards until you see the rate. Blackstone's funds bought in at a yield above 10%. That's what lenders charge a borrower they think is risky, and Blackstone has been getting paid that premium since it wrote the check.

The way the deal works is kind of clever. Anthropic needs $63 billion worth of Google's AI chips. Instead of borrowing all that itself, a separate company buys the chips and rents them to Anthropic, and the rent pays the lenders back. Broadcom, which has a strong A rating, guarantees more than $42 billion of it. Only about $18 billion depends on Anthropic
alone, and Blackstone took half of that.

The part I'd actually watch is the structure. Most of this financing leans on Broadcom's balance sheet, and Broadcom's own filing says the business depends on Anthropic's continued commercial success. Revenue jumped from $11.5 billion to $16.8 billion in a single quarter. As long as that keeps going, BB is probably a pit stop on the way to investment grade.
The scary version is growth stalling while $18 billion of debt sits on a company its own lenders already priced as junk.

evidence.quote: 1. The Hegotá upgrade will set the tone.
This upgrade will make Ethereum cryptographically agile.

EIP-8141, lovingly known as “Frames,” changes Ethereum accounts at the root level so that transaction validations can be programmable instead of tied to the ECSDA key (the thing Justin is warning people about in his post). Essentially accounts can choose how to authenticate instead of being tied to the current status quo. There are a few quantum proof

signatures out there like ML-DSA and SPHINCS, with frames you can choose whatever and also be open to even more gigabrain ones to come. When you are faced with a threat, agility is key, and Hegotá sets the tone for that agility.
2. The J* upgrade will produce a MVP quantum proof L1.
Think of J* as answering “what are the minimal changes Ethereum needs to make if quantum computers exist tomorrow?”
The goal here is to have enough to survive Q-day. Today, this maps to achieving a PQ heartbeat on consenus layers, leanDA PQ sampling, and leanSPHINCS transactions on execution.

If you’ve ever seen the strawmap (a proposed roadmap for Ethereum), you’ll know it has a lot of boxes. In particular, there is a quantum box. Also fun fact: it’s literally called a strawmap because it moves as research moves, and man is it moving!

evidence.quote: OneKey创始人：iPhone 11及更早机型存在无法修复的芯片漏洞，不宜存放助记词
iPhone 11及更早机型的BootROM存在checkm8、usbliter8等硬件漏洞，无法通过系统更新修复。攻击者只需物理接触设备，即可通过特制USB设备在系统启动前执行代码，飞行模式无效，且设备表面无异常。
Yishi建议相关用户生成全新助记词并转移资产，仅在旧助记词下新建地址无效。

The people I actually want to warn are those using an old iPhone as a cold wallet. iPhone 4S through iPhone X have checkm8 in the BootROM, made public in 2019. This June, usbliter8 went public, covering the iPhone XS, XR, the 11 series and the 2nd-gen SE. The BootROM is boot code burned into the chip at the factory. Apple can't patch it with a software

update, so these devices will carry the hole for as long as they exist. Exploiting it doesn't need a network either. Once someone has your phone in hand, they put it into DFU mode and plug in a custom USB board (the public research used a $5 Raspberry Pi Pico 2), and they can run their own code before iOS even boots. Airplane mode makes no difference here.

I don't want to overstate it. On models like the XS and 11, the BootROM bug alone won't hand over your seed phrase, because your passcode and the Secure Enclave are still in the way. The trouble is that these remaining layers are exactly where people tend to cut corners: a 6-digit passcode, an iOS version years out of date with a pile of public n-days, a

2. If you've already stored one there, no need to panic. When you get a chance, generate a brand-new seed phrase in an environment you trust and move your assets over. It has to be a whole new seed. A fresh address under the old seed won't help.

items.summary: Eth Research研究解码以太坊9个PropAMM 30天成交：多个场所在合约层强制同区块报价，吞单方成本约0.45bp且无逆向选择迹象；套利者常以PropAMM为新鲜报价腿，交易滞后的Uniswap等AMM。
items.author: ethresearchbot
items.new_information: 吞单成本约0.45bp且无逆向选择，PropAMM常作为套利的新鲜报价腿

evidence.quote: - Across 30 days the author decoded 92,627 fills on nine Ethereum PropAMM venues (69,827 WETH/stablecoin fills) and benchmarked execution quality using Binance 1-second trades as the external reference price.

- Several venues enforce quote freshness at the smart-contract level: for El Zorro, bopAMM, and Kipseli, the registry is read with minTimestamp=maxTimestamp=block.timestamp, so fills can only execute against maker updates from the same block (Tempest allows a small timestamp window).

- Execution costs are small and stable: takers lose about 0.45 bp at the fill on every day, and average markouts do not improve over the next 5 minutes for any taker class—showing no evidence of adverse selection against takers.

- After short-term CEX moves (>0.5 bp in the prior 12 seconds), 78.5% of fills trade against the move; PropAMM quotes adjust in the same block while Uniswap lags, so arbitrageurs/routers commonly use PropAMMs as the “fresh” leg versus “stale” AMMs.
